story.title: Book of Bhoots
paragraphs_en: What wanders outside on this dark and moonless night? What howls from the treetops, and whispers your name in the wind?
Maybe nothing. Maybe something. It depends on where you are. It depends on what you believe.
Keep an eye on the ponds and rivers. The Baak lives here. The Baak has twisted arms and legs, and its eyes and mouth are on its tummy. BAAK
If you meet a Baak, don’t worry. It is more interested in stealing raw fish than in scaring you. KHACH KHACH KHACH
Don’t look up at the skies at night. The Jilaiya flies like a bird when it’s dark. It sleeps when the sun shines. JILAIYA
If you meet a Jilaiya, don’t let it hear your name. It will suck your blood. Shooop Shooop Shooop
Watch out for palm trees. That’s where the Yakshi lives. She floats above the ground and is always thirsty. She takes her victims home and, the next day, there are bones under her tree. YAKSHI
If you meet a Yakshi, tell her not to come to tea. Kuchal Kuchal Kuchal
Be careful when you walk near railway tracks. The Skondhokata wanders here. He has lost his head in a horrible way. Ouch! He is looking for what he has lost. SKONDHOKATA
If you meet a Skondhokata, he will ask you to search for his head too. Chook Chook Chook
Beware the misty mountains. The Rantas works her dark magic here. She has long toenails and hair down to her knees, and her feet are turned backwards. RANTAS
If you meet a Rantas, don’t go with her. You will never come back. Phish Phish Phish
Stay alert in the desert. The Ret Ro Pret hides here. It uses sand to change itself. One day a brown hill, the next day a wave in the sand. RET RO PRET
If you travel to the desert, don’t wear browns and yellows. This sandy spirit will attack you. Sssss Sssss Sssss
Keep away from moving lights in forests. The Kolli Devva lurks here. He walks through the night with a wooden torch, and dances and troubles travellers. KOLLI DEVVA
If an invisible hand tries to light your lamp, scream and run. Cham Cham Cham
So what wails outside your window on this black night? You decide.
Maybe it’s a bird that sucks blood. Maybe it’s a woman with feet turned backwards. Maybe it’s the wind in an angry mood.
